contract: Restore the cached initial progress update when a warm source synchronously emits during start. Each selected or retried attempt has a subscription; later packets and later uses of the same source must continue to work. Record every accepted event once after decode completes, even if its visit has closed. Show progress only for the current visit. Preserve transfer cancellation, accepted retry and navigation ownership, cleanup, queued notices, and the existing queue-record format. Starting the source can invoke a callback before start returns; the candidate calls start before listen.

claims.statement: A warm source fails to show initial progress until a later packet arrives.
Subscription attachment calls start before registering its listener, so a synchronous event emitted by start has no listener from that attachment.
An event accepted before a visit closes must still be audited once when decoding finishes; a closed visit must stop receiving visible progress.
Repair must preserve the accepted retry's entry visit and synchronous queue record despite cancellation callbacks that navigate.

unknowns: No evidence establishes lazy cancellation consumption, asynchronous retry resumption, deferred batching, or a boundary persistence policy for the progress fix.
The source does not establish how the host handles listener registration or cleanup if a synchronous callback reenters during subscription attachment.
